mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS declining for 3+ months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.25% and remains there for at least one month, it signals a near-zero interest rate environment that encourages risk-taking in equity markets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.25% for 1 month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and a rise in the unemployment rate signals a monetary policy response to a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a stock market rebound as investors anticipate further stimulus and economic support, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market weakness
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction term has negative coefficient and p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high consumer spending and housing starts, a sustained increase in residential sales (RSAFS) signals strong demand for goods and services, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion with RSAFS above 12-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate over the past 6 months indicates a tightening labor market that increases corporate profit margins through higher productivity and wage growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with UNRATE declining for 6+ months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 5.0% and remains there for at least two months, it signals a tight labor market that accelerates wage growth and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with UNRATE < 5.0% for 2 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a shift in economic activity from construction to manufacturing, which typically boosts corporate earnings in the industrial sector and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls, or the interaction term has negative coefficient and p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime characterized by low industrial production growth, a decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO) signals potential supply chain disruptions that lead to higher inflation and corporate cost pressures, which typically cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during supply constraint with INDPRO below 100, or Rank IC > -0.03 over 3-year windows.
